ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, directors, officers and authorized signatories against: (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) the Canadian Sanctions List issued by Global Affairs Canada under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; (iii) FINTRAC's domestic and foreign Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) definition under PCMLTFA and associated regulations; and (iv) the OFAC SDN List for any USD-denominated maritime transactions. Enhanced due diligence is triggered for PEPs, vessel buyers, charterers, or any beneficial owner from FATF-identified high-risk jurisdictions. All negative-hit screening results must be documented and retained in the corporate records.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online (bcregistry.ca) operated by BC Registries and Online Services.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A corporate name may be in English, French, or a combined English-French form, and must be expressed in Latin characters. If a name is submitted in a non-Latin script or a foreign language, a certified transliteration into Latin characters must accompany the name request. The name must not misdescribe the business under BCBCA ss. 22-23, and the name must include a legal element such as 'Inc.', 'Corp.', 'Ltd.' or 'Company'.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the BC Registrar of Companies issues a written rejection notice with reasons. Within 30 days of the rejection, an administrative appeal may be filed through BC Corporate Online or by letter to the Registrar, attaching the original NUANS name search report, legal arguments, and any required regulatory consent. The appeal fee is CAD 25 (approx. USD 18). The Registrar will review and issue a decision within 15 business days. A rejected name may be re-submitted as a new request; name reservations are not formally extended but a new reservation may be filed upon expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office address is permissible solely for the registered office and records office under s. 26 of the BCBCA, provided a physical BC address is maintained for service of process and statutory records. However, for an ISIC 3011 commercial shipyard, the virtual office cannot serve as the operational shipyard; the corporation must maintain a physical production facility with municipal zoning approval, environmental registration, and Transport Canada works authorization. Industry-specific physical commercial premises are therefore mandatory for active vessel construction.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 75% likelihood of an unannounced physical on-site inspection during the first two years after active shipyard operations commence, and approximately 40% likelihood during the pre-incorporation/pre-production phase due to municipal business-licence inspections, environmental site assessments, and provincial occupational health and safety checks.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (British Columbia), SBC 2002, c. 57, ss. 10 (incorporation), 12 (articles), 14 (notice of articles), 21 (certificate of incorporation), and 31 (share capital); supplemented by the Business Corporations Regulation, B.C. Reg. 358/2004. The provincial BCBCA regime is the operative framework for this entity; federal continuance under the Canada Business Corporations Act is elective and not required.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: BC Registry Services, Corporate Online Division, Service BC, on behalf of the Ministry of Finance, Province of British Columbia
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notice of Articles (Form 1) and Articles of Incorporation filed electronically through the BC Corporate Online portal, resulting in the issuance of the Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow deposit is prescribed under the BCBCA. Authorized share capital is fixed in the Articles; the initial subscription may be satisfied in cash, property, or past services at a nominal value (e.g., CAD $0.01 per share). No provincial escrow account is mandated; however, federal shipbuilding program eligibility (e.g., National Shipbuilding Strategy) may impose Canadian beneficial ownership and performance-escrow conditions on a project basis.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION NO. 1 OF [CORPORATION NAME] RESOLVED that the Corporation accepts the Incorporator's subscription for 1,000 Class A voting common shares at CAD $1.00 per share and issues them upon receipt of full consideration. RESOLVED that the registered and records office is fixed at [suite, street, city], British Columbia. RESOLVED that the directors approve the appointment of [director A] as President/Chief Executive Officer, [director B] as Secretary, and [director C] as Chief Financial Officer, each holding office until the next annual general meeting or until successors are appointed. RESOLVED FURTHER that the directors authorize all filings and fee payments necessary to complete incorporation under the Business Corporations Act (British Columbia).

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services – Corporate Online Portal (Service BC, Ministry of Finance)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a corporate name request through the BC Corporate Online portal; the system performs a NUANS-based preliminary examination of the proposed name against existing BC and federal corporate registers. Reserve the approved name for a maximum of 56 days, extendable by subsequent request. If the name is deemed available, proceed directly to draft the Notice of Articles using the exact reserved name.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director (Form 2) of each proposed director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is rejected as indistinguishable or deceiving, file an amended name request or submit a written reconsideration application supported by legal argument, a new name search, and evidence of distinctiveness within the applicable 21-business-day response window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Formation Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate solicitor or authorized service agent; execution before a notary public or witness per BCBCA signing rules
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Notice of Articles (Form 1), Articles (Form 5 or custom compliant form), and the Incorporator's declaration. Execute the Articles by the Incorporator; each proposed director must sign a Consent to Act as Director on or before incorporation. For non-resident signatories, arrange notarized execution or apostilled signature blocks where required. Verify that the Articles set the authorized class of shares, special rights, transfer restrictions, and first director roster consistent with the corporate plan.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director (Form 2) for each director
Registered and records office address particulars
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: The registry will issue a formal defect notification if the filed documents omit statutory particulars; cure by correcting the offending electronic form and resubmitting via Corporate Online within the cure window. Ministerial corrections to rejected filings do not attract a new fee; substantively amended filings require a fresh submission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Submission of Incorporation Application and Fee Payment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services – Corporate Online Portal (servicebc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed Notice of Articles and Articles into Corporate Online; attach the directors' consents; validate all statutory fields; pay the CAD $350 incorporation fee (plus any applicable expedited processing fee) by credit card or pre-authorized electronic payment; retain the filing acknowledgement and transaction reference for follow-up.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On a query or rejection notice, the applicant receives a defect report listing missing particulars; deliver the corrected schedules within the prescribed 14-calendar-day cure period, failing which the filing is deemed void and a new submission with applicable fee is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the Certificate of Incorporation and Establishing the Corporate Minute Book
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services and the corporation's registered solicitor
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, download the electronic Certificate of Incorporation and the filed registry extract from Corporate Online. Prepare the corporate minute book containing the Certificate, Notice of Articles, Articles, the First Board Resolution, Consents to Act, registers of directors and shareholders, and blank share certificates. Issue Class A voting common share certificates to the subscriber in accordance with the adopted First Board Resolution; have officers affix the corporate seal where the Articles require a seal.
required_dossiers: Registered extract from BC Corporate Registry
Share certificates and stock transfer ledger
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Clerical errors in the Certificate (e.g., typographical variance in the corporate name) are corrected by filing a registrar's correction application under the BCBCA; substantive changes require a special resolution amending the Articles and a new Notice of Articles.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Business Number, Tax Account Registration, and Banking Facilities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online (BRO)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Enroll the corporation at CRA Business Registration Online using the Certificate of Incorporation and Notice of Articles data. Obtain the nine-digit Business Number (BN), registrations for GST/HST (5% federal GST; shipbuilding export sales are generally zero-rated), corporate income tax, and payroll source deductions. Open the corporate operating account and the maritime installment letter-of-credit/escrow facility at a Schedule I Canadian bank, and submit the standard know-your-client corporate banking package.
required_dossiers: Directors' government-issued identification and residency declarations
Proof of registered office (lease or utility invoice)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA registration returns a data mismatch, resubmit the corrected RC159 through My Business Account or request manual verification at the CRA Business Window, providing the certified corporate registry extract and director identification to expedite reconciliation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registered Office Maintenance, Annual Reports, and Statutory Governance Filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: BC Registry Services Corporate Online and Canada Revenue Agency
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Maintain the registered and records office at a visible physical address in British Columbia. File the BCBCA annual report within two months of the anniversary of incorporation and pay the CAD $38 annual registry fee. File the T2 corporate income tax return within six months of the fiscal year-end and GST/HST returns as applicable. Update the Notice of Articles within 10 days of any change to directors, officers, or the registered office, and convene the annual general meeting as required by the BCBCA and the corporation's bylaws.
required_dossiers: BC annual report filing via Corporate Online
Updated Notice of Articles on director or office changes
T2 corporate income tax return and provincial schedules
Annual general meeting minutes and director election records
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filings incur administrative penalties and, after two consecutive missed years, the Registrar may strike the company off the register; cure by filing all outstanding returns and fees, and if struck off, apply under the BCBCA for restoration and reinstatement with proof of good standing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Transport Canada Marine Safety and Security Directorate (federal) and Technical Safety BC (provincial technical regulator for lifting equipment, pressure equipment, and boilers); worksite safety oversight by WorkSafeBC
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Shipyard Vessel Construction and Industrial Operating Permit under the Canada Shipping Act, 2001 (vessel construction survey and safety certification) and the Technical Safety BC Industrial Equipment Operating Permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Impact Assessment Agency of Canada (federal, under the Impact Assessment Act, S.C. 2019, c. 28) and the BC Environmental Assessment Office (provincial, under the Environmental Assessment Act, S.B.C. 2002, c. 43); Vancouver Fraser Port Authority if the shipyard footprint occupies federal port lands
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B - Screening-level site-specific environmental assessment and Waste Discharge Authorization under the BC Environmental Management Act; a full EIA (comprehensive impact assessment report) is mandatory where the shipyard is designated under the federal Impact Assessment Act or meets the thresholds of the BC Reviewable Projects Regulation (e.g., large marine terminal/shipbuilding facilities with berth length or production capacity above prescribed limits).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: prohibition of deleterious discharges under s. 36(3) of the Fisheries Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. F-14; BC effluent authorizations require BOD <= 45 mg/L and TSS <= 60 mg/L monthly average, pH 6.0-9.0, and no visible oil sheen. Emissions: CEPA facility air pollutant reporting and Canadian marine coating VOC content limits (<= 420 g/L for ship hull paints); abrasive blasting debris and hazardous wastes must be containerized, manifested, and disposed under the BC Contaminated Sites Regulation and the Transportation of Dangerous Goods Act. Ambient noise and dust must comply with applicable municipal by-laws.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal or port fire authority inspection and BC Fire Code compliance certification for fabrication shops, dry docks, and berthing areas; Technical Safety BC structural load and pressure equipment inspection certificates for gantry cranes, slipways, and lifting gear; WorkSafeBC occupational health and safety registration and worksite clearance certificate under the Workers Compensation Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c. 492; Transport Canada marine safety clearance for vessel launch and sea trials.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC); applicable federal tax portal: CRA My Business Account and Business Registration Online at www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html. The British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST) is administered by the Consumer Taxation Branch of the BC Ministry of Finance; relevant portal: BC eTaxBC at etax.gov.bc.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Canadian Business Corporation must obtain a Canada Revenue Agency Business Number (BN), which serves as the unified identifier for income tax, GST/HST, payroll, and customs/import-export accounts. Apply by filing CRA Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number), by telephone through CRA Business Registration, or by electronic registration through CRA Business Registration Online / BizRegister BC. A BC PST vendor number must be obtained separately through eTaxBC before making PST-taxable sales in British Columbia. For a newly formed federal or BC corporation, the incorporating authority supplies the corporate registration number, which is distinct from the CRA BN; the corporation should be registered for GST/HST if its worldwide taxable supplies exceed the CAD 30,000 small-supplier threshold or if it wishes to claim input tax credits on export-related inputs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election. A Business Corporation is legally classified as a separate taxable entity and assessed at the corporate entity level; no pass-through election is available. Canadian domestic law and the Canada-US tax treaty use legal residence and place of effective management rather than a flexible elective classification. Hybrid mismatch rules in the Income Tax Act operate automatically to deny deductions or require inclusion for payments giving rise to deduction-without-inclusion outcomes; there is no elective hybrid-mismatch opt-in. Limited statutory elections available to a corporation include choosing a non-calendar taxation year under Income Tax Act section 249.1 and, where applicable, filing under section 216 for non-resident income of a passive nature, which is not the operating classification for an active vessel construction shipyard.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) at the federal level, supplemented by the British Columbia Provincial Sales Tax (PST); Canada does not operate a unified VAT or a single combined sales tax system.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: GST/HST registration threshold: CAD 30,000 of taxable supplies (including zero-rated supplies) earned in Canada over the immediately preceding four consecutive calendar quarters; once exceeded, GST/HST registration is mandatory. BC PST: no comparable general small-supplier threshold; a vendor making taxable sales in British Columbia must obtain a PST number and collect, remit, and administer PST obligations. The combined nominal BC retail rate is 12% (5% federal GST plus 7% BC PST), but an export sale of an oceangoing vessel may be zero-rated for GST/HST and exempt from BC PST if all prescribed export conditions are met.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not currently impose real-time fiscal clearance, API-based tax authority approval, or digital stamping for GST/HST/PST invoices. Electronic invoicing is permitted if the invoice is generated, retained, and accessible in a clear and legible format. CRA requires a GST/HST registrant to issue invoices containing prescribed information for taxable supplies, including zero-rated export supplies, and to keep all source documents, customs records, bills of lading, and payment evidence available for audit. BC PST invoices must substantiate exemptions such as export sales and, for a vessel export, should include the buyer's non-resident status, delivery terms, export destination, and supporting export documentation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A commercial shipyard supplying a newly built ocean container vessel to a non-resident purchaser may claim zero-rating under Part V of Schedule VI to the Excise Tax Act when the supply is an export of tangible personal property. The conditions include: (i) title and risk in the vessel pass to the non-resident purchaser; (ii) the vessel is delivered to a common carrier, freight forwarder, or other export agent for carriage out of Canada, or is physically sailed or towed out of Canadian waters promptly after delivery; (iii) the vessel is not used or consumed in Canada before export; (iv) the shipyard obtains and retains documentary evidence showing the vessel left Canada and was delivered to the foreign buyer; and (v) the supply is reported as a zero-rated export on the GST/HST return. Where the vessel is constructed under contract for a non-resident buyer and title transfers abroad, the construction services may also qualify for zero-rating as a supply to a non-resident if the service is performed on tangible movable property destined for export. For BC PST, a sale of goods to be exported out of British Columbia is generally exempt when the vendor obtains an export declaration or equivalent evidence that the vessel was exported from Canada within the applicable period; without such evidence, BC PST may be assessed on the full sale price.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (CBSA Canadian Export Declaration / eManifest export report filed by the shipyard or authorised customs broker)
Bill of Lading (ocean or through bill of lading evidencing the vessel's carriage from Canada to the non-resident purchaser)
Inward Remittance Certificate (or equivalent bank SWIFT MT103 / foreign exchange credit evidence demonstrating payment repatriation by the non-resident buyer)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and the BC Ministry of Finance apply strict documentation-based scrutiny to zero-rated export claims. If the required export evidence is not timely produced, CRA may reverse the zero-rating, reassess the vessel sale at 5% GST (and potentially impose BC PST under provincial law), issue a clawback of input tax credits, and assess interest. Normal GST/HST reassessments generally occur within four years; the period is unlimited where the export claim involves misrepresentation, fraud, or wilful default. Penalties can include a gross-negligence penalty equal to 50% of the misstated net tax or refund, a false-statement penalty, BC PST penalty and interest, and criminal prosecution for GST/HST evasion under the Excise Tax Act. Exporters are expected to retain all export bills, customs acknowledgements, proof of foreign payment, and foreign-exchange repatriation records for at least six years to avoid penalties and retrospective clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full current and capital account convertibility; no exchange controls on profit remittance or capital movements. Non-resident shareholders may repatriate dividends and capital subject to Part XIII withholding and applicable tax treaty relief. CAD/USD/EUR trade freely in the interbank market; no Canadian restriction on holding foreign-currency accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender obligation or mandatory conversion ratio; export proceeds may be retained in foreign-currency accounts. FINTRAC reporting applies to cross-border electronic fund transfers equal to or exceeding CAD 10,000; Canadian customs export reporting under the Customs Act and Statistics Act is required for vessel deliveries.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Trade Finance and LC Unit
Operational Account / Escrow for Instalment Collections

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility with legal constraints. Offshore EMIs (e.g., Wise, Airwallex, Currencycloud) may be used as collection agents and low-value operational payment conduits, but cannot support maritime LC issuance, escrow settlement, or deposit-taking in Canada. They are required to register as money services businesses (MSB) under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and with FINTRAC for any Canadian-facing remittance activity; British Columbia requires extra-provincial registration. For Stage 4 treasury operations, EMIs should be limited to non-critical operational transfers and must be backed by a Canadian bank-grade clearing rail for capital injections and trade settlements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permissible for a BC Business Corporation, but signatories may be required to appear virtually or through notarized identification where the bank's client acceptance policy demands enhanced diligence. For 'Medium-Risk Enhanced' commercial shipbuilders, banks may impose a physical interview with at least one director or authorised officer, especially when a principal beneficial owner is a non-resident. Certified government-issued IDs, proof of address, a recorded video call, and banking references are standard prerequisites.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex ownership structure with non-resident shareholders and foreign intermediate holdings.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified BC corporate registry extract; foreign corporate extracts; organizational chart; UBO declaration for every shareholder holding 25% or more; passport copies; board resolution authorizing account opening; notarized source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statement covering the shipyard investment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Trade-based money laundering red flags in vessel sales: progress payment mismatch or over-invoicing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed shipbuilding contract (ISIC 3011), payment and draw schedule, independent marine surveyor valuation, IMO/class registration, commercial invoice set, bill of lading and cargo documents, customs export declarations, and an economic rationale memo for each instalment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Escrow account usage for client instalments is high-risk for fronting or diversion.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Escrow agreement among bank, shipyard, and client; AML/KYC documentation on all settled beneficiaries; segregation attestation from external auditor; anti-criminal diversion certification; internal AML/ATF compliance policy and designated compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure in export contract or freight route.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UN, US, OSFI, and OFAC sanctions screening results; end-user and end-use assurance certificate; export permit under the Export and Import Permits Act (if applicable); vessel geolocation and cargo manifest; foreign policy risk analysis.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 with a dedicated remittance field identifying 'EQUITY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION'; beneficiary account at a Canadian Schedule I bank; verify beneficial owner and source of funds; attach share subscription, board resolution, updated British Columbia notice of alteration, and share register; FINTRAC EFT report required for amounts at or above CAD 10,000; no foreign-exchange control permit or Bank of Canada approval required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Use SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier vendor payments; use SWIFT MT700 / MT710 plus Commercial LC for vessel-equipment instalments and hull construction progress drawdowns; provide invoice, packing list, bill of lading, certificate of origin, and milestone certificates; all cross-border EFTs exceeding CAD 10,000 are reported to FINTRAC.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla FX call/put option (CAD/USD and CAD/EUR quoted by a Schedule I bank)
Non-deliverable forward (NDF for illiquid exotic currencies, if trade exposure exists)
FX corridor and participating forward (risk-reversal option structure)

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: BC Annual Report for Business Corporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, British Columbia Registry Services, Ministry of Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 2 months after the anniversary date of the company's incorporation or continuation under the BC Business Corporations Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing fees apply immediately after the 2-month filing period; continued non-filing for two consecutive years subjects the corporation to administrative dissolution under the BC Business Corporations Act, which terminates its capacity to perform vessel construction contracts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership and Transparency Register Annual Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of Companies, British Columbia Corporate Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed concurrently with the BC Annual Report within the same 2-month anniversary window; share-transfer updates must be recorded in the register when the company receives notice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors who knowingly fail to maintain or confirm beneficial ownership information may be subject to offence penalties; continued annual non-compliance supports administrative strike-off and dissolution proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return and Required Financial Schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due no later than 6 months after fiscal year-end; balance-due day is 2 months after year-end for non-CCPCs and 3 months after year-end for CCPCs eligible for the small business deduction
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-file penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per full month up to 12 months; repeat penalty surcharges apply; gross negligence penalties up to 50% of understatement and prescribed arrears interest may be assessed.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold under the BC Business Corporations Act. Mandatory audit applies to reporting issuers under securities legislation and to companies whose articles or unanimous shareholder agreement require an audit. A private BC corporation may waive the appointment of an auditor by unanimous shareholder resolution each financial year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public and reporting issuers must use IFRS. Private BC companies may elect Canadian ASPE or IFRS for financial statements; corporate tax reporting is computed under the Income Tax Act with CRA-specific reconciliations.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Once a year, before filing the annual report, directors must audit the corporate registers: reconcile the Register of Members against share transfers, update the Register of Directors, and verify the Beneficial Ownership and Transparency Register for each individual with significant control. The signed annual confirmation states that all registers are complete and accurate; any deficiency discovered is corrected before the filing is submitted.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 170-550 per year for BC registered office and records office services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000-18,500 for a certified independent audit of a commercial shipyard company, subject to inventory valuation and bank covenants
